reflections.title: Called Sons of the Living God

reflect.text: God told the prophet Hosea to enter a painful marriage with an unfaithful woman named Gomer. Hosea chose faithful obedience over his personal comfort, even though it brought public mockery and deep grief. His broken home became a living picture of God's relationship with Israel. The people had abandoned the Lord for false gods, and the names of Hosea's children pointed to coming judgment, lost pity, and national rejection.

Even in this dark warning, God revealed His amazing kindness. He promised to rescue His people by His own mercy, without bows, swords, or human soldiers, so that the glory would belong entirely to Him. What is more, God promised that those who heard the sad words 'not My people' would become children of the living God. As F. B. Meyer observed, God took us into a covenant 'not because we were good, but to make us so.' No one is beyond the reach of His restoring grace.

questions: How does knowing that God welcomed us when we were unfaithful change the way you trust Him today?
Are there areas where you are relying on human strength rather than resting in God's mercy?
reflections.prayer: Father, thank You for loving us even when our hearts have wandered away from You. We praise You for saving us by Your own power and adopting us as Your dearly loved children. Help us to follow Your call with patience, and teach us to depend entirely on Your grace. Amen.

D5.author: D. A. Carson
D5.work: Read the Bible: 2 Kings 9, 1 Timothy 6, Hosea 1, and Psalm 119:73–96
